I read the whole file and searched Mathlib for competing versions of its concepts. Results:
- `PowerSeries.log` is the only formal power series logarithm. The other `log` declarations in Mathlib are the analytic `Real.log`/`Complex.log` results and their series expansions in `Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log`. Those are real-analytic functions, not a power-series object over a ℚ-algebra, so `PowerSeries.log` does not duplicate them.
- `derivative_log` reuses the existing `mk_neg_one_pow_mul_one_add_eq_one` from `WellKnown.lean`. The geometric series `mk fun n ↦ (-1)^n` is not given a new definition.
- `logOf` is a thin named wrapper around `(log A).subst (f - 1)`. It adds `constantCoeff_logOf`, `logOf_one_add_X` and `logOf_exp`, so it is a useful named specialisation and not a competing concept.
- `eq_of_derivative_mul_one_add_X_eq_self` is a standalone lemma built on `derivative.ext`. Theorem-level duplication is outside this rubric.
- The two `HasSubst` lemmas are theorems, not parallel structures.
I found no avoidable duplicate of an existing Mathlib, Batteries or core concept. The only uncertainty is that my search was by name and pattern, so an unrelated parallel definition under different naming could have been missed.
